main_body: A tall strip of wooden fence posts and rails (farm fence). Each post is a block with a tan top and an orange-brown front. Dark vertical plank sections and thin grey rails sit between the posts.
top_band: Tan/light-orange cap at rows ~0-3 on each post block, about 3 rows tall and only on the small post. The dark plank sections and grey rails have no top band.
evidence: Only the small post caps show a top. The main frame elements, the horizontal rails (grey, 2-3 rows, e.g. rows 14-15, 31-32, 46-47) and the dark plank sections, are drawn as flat front-facing bands with no visible top surface. There is no distinct front-edge line, eave shadow or inset. The guide treats a frame whose beams and base lack top faces as a front elevation with a hat, so this fails.

style.evidence: The posts have about 4 wood steps (tan, orange, brown, dark brown) and dark-brown outlines that follow the material. The dark plank columns and the grey rails are large flat fills with little grain. The pattern repeats with little per-tile variation, so it is thinner than the roofed well and the cheese stall, which carry 5-6 steps and dense texture.
